items.title: Typical energy bill forecast to go up by £443 a year from January as inflation rate rises again
items.summary: Energy bills are expected to jump by 26% a year for a typical household as UK inflation hits its highest rate for a year.
items.body: Gas and electricity bills for a typical household are forecast to jump by £443 a year from January as the inflation rate rose to its highest level in a year. A typical annual bill is predicted to rise by 26% in the new year, according to consultancy Cornwall Insight, ahead of the official announcement next week. Some households will get a £100 payment to help with the rising cost of living, a policy which was announced in the Budget. Prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September mainly because of higher petrol and diesel prices, official figures show. Inflation has been driven higher in recent months as the US-Israel war with Iran has driven up the cost of energy and fuel. In response to prices surging, the Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in three years earlier this month, in a bid to slow inflation to its target of 2%.

items.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6% after petrol and diesel prices hit record high
items.summary: Increase in October piles pressure on households as Iran war pushes up oil cost and rattles global economy Energy bills in Great Britain forecast to rise by 26% to £2,166 from January Inflation in the UK rose to 3.6% in October after petrol prices increased and diesel hit a…
items.body: Inflation in the UK rose to 3.6% in October after petrol prices increased and diesel hit a record high amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East. Figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) show the headline rate of inflation as measured by the consumer prices index rose from 3.5% in September and was in line with City economists’ forecasts. As households brace for the colder winter months with household gas and electricity costs soaring, the latest figures push the headline inflation rate to the highest level in a year. In a reading underscoring the pressure on the Bank of England to raise interest rates, the ONS said fuel prices were the major contributor. Annual costs of raw materials and goods leaving factories also continued to climb, driven by rising energy and crude oil prices amid the Iran war.

items.body: Energy bills across Great Britain are predicted to reach £2,166 a year for the typical household from January as the impact of the Middle East conflict piles pressure on the government to offer more support to hard-hit households. The government’s cap on gas and electricity prices is likely to rise by 26% early next year, equivalent to adding £443 to the average annual dual-fuel bill, in one of the biggest quarterly price rises on record, according to the leading forecaster Cornwall Insight. The dire prediction for millions of hard-pressed households marks the final forecast before the industry regulator for Great Britain, Ofgem , sets electricity and gas rates for the coldest months of the year from January through to March via a new energy price cap next Wednesday.

items.title: Risks from AI valuations, fiscal imbalances and geoeconomic tensions weigh on financial stability outlook
items.body: The outlook for euro area financial stability is being shaped by risks stemming from artificial intelligence (AI) valuations, fiscal imbalances and geoeconomic tensions, according to the November 2026 Financial Stability Review , which is published today by the European Central Bank (ECB). “Risks to euro area financial stability remain elevated, given persistent geoeconomic uncertainty and growing exposure to AI,” said ECB Vice-President Boris Vujčić. “Banks are well placed to withstand shocks, while vulnerabilities are more pronounced in certain non-banks where risks are growing and macroprudential safeguards are less developed.” The euro area economy has continued to demonstrate resilience despite an energy shock, trade frictions and extreme weather events. Prolonged energy supply disruptions and persistent trade policy uncertainty could, however, test this resilience.

items.title: Japan exports in October surge 20.5%, beating estimates on robust chip shipments
items.summary: Semiconductor shipments spiked almost 50% year on year.
items.body: Japan's exports in October surged 20.5% from a year earlier, snapping a two-month slowdown in shipments, official data released Wednesday showed. Exports growth beat expectations of economists polled by Reuters that had pegged it at 20%, and it was sharply higher compared to a revised 16.5% in September. Shipments of semiconductor equipment that have been propping up Tokyo's exports jumped 49.7% by value. Exports of motor vehicles climbed 19.9% year on year. In terms of destinations, shipments to China rose 13.3%, while they climbed 23.9% to the U.S. Exports have been the main driver of Japan's growth, although a surge in the value of imports of petroleum due to the Iran war has offset some the impact of the exports surge on its economy.

Fears of AI-powered cyberattacks, heightened by incidents like the Hugging Face breach, are driving demand for cybersecurity vendors like Palo Alto Networks. Palo Alto said annual recurring revenue for its next-generation security business jumped 66% from a year ago to $9.73 billion. items.title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave
items.summary: Europe hopes to be a leader in a new generation of computer chips which use light to process data.
items.body: "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO. If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger. The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical. They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre). Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips. Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.

items.summary: The Amazon chairman says he was originally "biased against" Pattinson "because he's already so famous".
items.body: Jeff Bezos has said he was "heavily involved" in casting Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond. Speaking at an event in California, the Amazon chairman said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson - who starred in many blockbuster films like Batman and the Twilight series - "because he's already so famous". The role of 007 has typically gone to an actor who is not as well known at the time of casting. But Bezos said in screen tests, "it was so obvious he is James Bond". This will be the first 007 film in the official series not under the creative control of the Broccoli family, who had overseen the franchise since the first movie in 1962. Amazon purchased MGM, which co-owns the franchise, in 2022. "There was something special about Rob", Bezos said at Semafor Silicon Valley & The World Event on Tuesday.

items.body: Ministers will drop plans to ban foie gras imports into the UK in order to smooth a trade deal with the EU that will be announced this week. As first reported by the Financial Times, the proposed ban will be officially dropped on Friday when the government announces its sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) trade deal with the EU to reduce checks and paperwork on imports and exports of food and drink with the bloc. Labour promised before coming to power that it would ban foie gras imports. Before the election, Steve Reed, the then shadow environment secretary, said Labour would “ban the commercial import of foie gras, where ducks and geese are aggressively force-fed”. He labelled the practice “beyond disgusting”.

items.title: Ford starts U.S. battery cell production using Chinese tech amid geopolitical tensions
items.summary: Ford has started U.S. production and shipments of battery cells for its next-generation EVs using technologies licensed by Chinese battery giant CATL.
items.body: MARSHALL, Mich. — Ford Motor has started producing battery cells in the U.S. for its next generation of electric vehicles using technologies licensed by Chinese battery giant CATL. The automaker said Wednesday that cell production at a $3 billion plant in Marshall, Michigan — roughly 100 miles west of Detroit — started last month and the cells are now shipping out. They'll be used in prototypes for its Fathom small electric pickup truck , which CEO Jim Farley has touted as rivaling Tesla and Chinese competitors. The production marks a milestone for the Detroit automaker and is the next step toward using lower-cost lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, battery cells in U.S. vehicles. The technology was created in the U.S. but commercialized largely in China.

items.body: Two new reports on the housing market show activity slowing even more, after a September spike in mortgage rates sent it into a deep freeze. Pending home sales in October dropped 4.7% month-over-month and were down 16.7% from October of last year, according to the National Association of Realtors. This is the lowest level in the index's 25-year history. Analysts had been looking for a much smaller decline, likely because mortgage rates pulled back slightly in October, only to rise sharply again last week. The average rate on the 30-year fixed started October at 7.54% according to Mortgage News Daily and ended the month at 7.27%. The pending count is based on signed contracts — people out shopping and signing deals during the month. It is therefore an indicator of future closed sales.

The proceedings in the southern tech hub of Shenzhen kicked off with a CEO Summit of business leaders on Tuesday, to be followed by an Economic Leaders' Meeting beginning Wednesday. On the sidelines, Xi and Trump are expected to have their third summit of the year as they seek to manage a fraught superpower rivalry. As the Ukraine war drags on and tensions with Iran simmer, all eyes are on a trilateral summit among Xi, Trump and Putin that the White House has said will happen on Thursday. items.title: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
items.summary: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
items.body: Further problems with the accuracy of speed cameras on English roads have been uncovered which may have allowed drivers to slip through the cracks and escape fines. National Highways discovered issues with speed cameras last year , affecting 154 out of 400 cameras but, following an investigation, said it had found another fault on units monitoring roads including those running between Huntingdon and Cambridge. The Home Office has revoked approval that allows footage from the cameras to be used as evidence in legal proceedings. US firm Verra Mobility operates the cameras but National Highways said it will now end the contract. "If we're going to prosecute people, we need to be confident the system is working as it should.

items.title: LeBron James sues sports betting app Bron for using nickname and likeness without permission
items.summary: NBA star’s lawsuit alleges ‘previously unknown app’ acted illegally ‘to gain notoriety’ by seeming affiliated with James LeBron James sued the sports betting research app Bron on Tuesday, accusing it of trademark infringement for using his nickname ⁠and an artificial…
items.body: LeBron James sued the sports betting research app Bron on Tuesday, accusing it of trademark infringement for using his nickname ⁠and an artificial intelligence-generated ⁠likeness of him in ​a recent ad campaign without permission. In a complaint filed in New York City federal court, the Philadelphia 76ers star, whose nickname is Bron, said he carefully protects his image and chooses who to endorse, reflecting his ⁠status as “one of the most recognizable identities in the world”, and commands tens of millions of dollars for endorsing products or ventures. The complaint asks the court to block the makers from using James’s name, to give up any money they have already made and to award damages – including fair market value for the use of his name as well as punitive damages.

items.title: Emergency alerts and $75,000 rewards: South Korea fights high-tech exam cheating
items.summary: South Korea moves to crack down on exam cheating with emergency alerts and $75,000 rewards.
items.body: South Korea plans to send emergency alerts to expose concealed phones, while offering rewards of at least $75,000 for reporting cheaters, as it gears for a key college entrance exam. The measures, announced by President Lee Jae Myung in a post on X, come ahead of the country's annual college entrance exam, known as the Suneung, on Thursday which is expected to draw about 550,000 students, according to local media reports. Emergency alerts are to be sent to mobile phones of all South Korean residents before the exam begins, aimed at identifying mobile phones that students fail to surrender, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Tuesday.

items.body: WASHINGTON/NEW YORK -- The opposition Democratic Party will hold a 56-44 majority in the U.S. Senate after winning the final unresolved race in Alaska, completing a sweeping midterm victory that also gave the party control of the House of Representatives. Democrat Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, according to The Associated Press, capping a nine-seat Democratic pickup that stretched into traditionally conservative states including Texas, Kansas, Mississippi and South Carolina. The result completes an election in which Democrats capitalized on widespread voter discontent over Republican President Donald Trump's policies on inflation, tariffs, AI data centers and the Iran war. items.title: Security flaw found in Java, world's third-largest programming language
items.summary: The same tech start-up that discovered a PHP flaw used AI to uncover a critical software bug in one of the world's most popular computer language programs.
items.body: A cyber-security firm has used artificial intelligence (AI) to uncover a critical flaw in the hugely popular computer programming language Java. Tech start-up Calif - which recently identified a cyber-security flaw in another language, PHP - found the bug in Java's memory functions. Java is a popular programming language used by nearly all of the world's top companies such as Apple and Amazon, as well as many banks, hospitals and governments. It is meant to make the IT world more secure by managing your memory online, said computer scientist Professor Toby Walsh, which is why "this is such an unlikely and serious flaw". The discovery comes after a string of serious technology issues, including a massive Microsoft outage . On Tuesday, the US National Security Agency said its internal communications went offline on Tuesday due to a "scheduled routine maintenance".

items.title: More gas storage is at risk. What’s the government plan for secure supplies?
items.summary: SSE’s threat to close a big storage facility in Yorkshire highlights successive governments’ failures to build a strategy and safeguard supplies Labour faces double blow over UK fossil fuel projects For those who followed the many months of government dithering over whether to…
items.body: F or those who followed the many months of government dithering over whether to approve production at the Jackdaw gasfield off the coast of Aberdeen, Scotland, there was a treat on social media this week. It was the sight of Michael Shanks, energy minister, almost dancing a jig of delight as the first output from Jackdaw flowed into the national gas network. “It will increase domestic production and further boost our energy security during the transition to electrification and decarbonisation,” he declared . To which the only possible response is: if the security benefit of using domestic gas during transition is so clear (and it is, as argued here from time to time ) why did it take a year of ministerial agonising before the inevitable thumbs up arrived? Still, you might think, at least the government now has a joined-up approach to gas.

items.summary: Ukraine's charge d'affaires to the U.S., Denys Sienik, said that Starshield had been speed-limited for seven days already in Ukraine.
items.body: SpaceX's military-grade satellite internet service is still operating under speed limits in parts of Ukraine, compromising the country's ability to defend itself against Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an X post on Tuesday. "The speed limit on Starshield in the temporarily occupied territories remains in place. We are discussing this with the American side," Zelenskyy wrote. He last week said Kyiv was investigating fresh restrictions on Starshield — developed by SpaceX for government use — over Ukraine, especially the front line and temporarily occupied territories.

items.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from all US freeways
items.summary: The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless vehicles from operating on the state's highways following a series of traffic incidents.
items.body: Waymo has temporarily suspended its driverless vehicles from operating on all US freeways, the company has said. The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless taxis from state freeways following a series of recent traffic incidents. California's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) cited an "imminent hazard to public safety" for the ban, noting an incident this month in which several driverless Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on US Route 101. Waymo said it was working with state officials "diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations", adding that no injuries or collisions were reported following the incident on US Route 101 south of San Francisco.

items.title: Energy price cap rise: how to switch providers
items.summary: It is possible to switch to a better tariff and save money despite the forecast rise next year Average energy bill in Great Britain predicted to rise to £2,166 The energy price cap in Great Britain looks likely to go up by 26% in January . But your bills might not have to rise…
items.body: The energy price cap in Great Britain looks likely to go up by 26% in January . But your bills might not have to rise by the same amount. If you are paying a tariff that matches the price cap you could save by switching to something lower. And if you do it now, you could make a substantial saving. Providers are offering fixed tariffs that work out up to £407 below the estimated price cap, according to price comparison website uSwitch. It’s worth noting that it’s the price of the energy you use that is fixed, not your bill – so you will still be charged according to what you use. The easiest way is to use a price comparison website such as Uswitch , GoCompare and The Energy Shop . They typically obtain a lot of information from suppliers so you need to provide very little to get a quote (you might be alarmed by how much data is on there).

items.title: Nvidia’s Kress faces a divided workforce as some employees push for Huang’s return
items.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress calmed investors. Now she has to calm employees.
items.body: The day before Colette Kress led her first earnings call as Nvidia's interim CEO, she did not want to talk about her predecessor, Jensen Huang . "This is a new era for Nvidia," she told employees in an internal meeting on Monday, according to a person present, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. When someone brought up Huang, Kress quickly changed the subject, according to the person. On Wednesday, Kress addressed the whole company at the first Nvidia all-hands meeting since the public chaos over Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and other reported relationships. And while Kress will be tasked with filling the leadership vacuum created by Huang's departure, she is also tamping down public calls to bring him back. Huang himself weighed in with his first public statement Tuesday saying he would be "honored" to return to Nvidia.

items.title: As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal
items.summary: China worries the scandal could ramp up pressure on the US to further restrict the sale of advanced chips.
items.body: Jensen Huang is out but his shadow looms over the upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping this week. For Beijing, the former Nvidia CEO's dramatic fall is a major challenge - and not just because of claims that a Chinese spy may have honey-trapped Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry's most influential figures. Rather, the allegations surrounding Huang and his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang are turning into a new flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship. US intelligence reports claim she had ties to Beijing's intelligence apparatus - in particular the Ministry of State Security, China's main civilian spy agency.

items.title: The reboot of poor Jensen Huang almost worked. But who can explain away 30 leather jackets? | Emma Brockes
items.summary: He seemed like the thinking person’s tech titan. But then came the affairs, the share collapse – and of course, the sorry items in his wardrobe A few years ago, I attended a small dinner at a friend’s house in the US at which a tech billionaire was the guest of honour. He wasn’t…
items.body: A few years ago, I attended a small dinner at a friend’s house in the US at which a tech billionaire was the guest of honour. He wasn’t one of the most famous tech billionaires – I’d never heard of him, although I used his communications platform every day. Nonetheless, it was exciting to get up close to someone that staggeringly rich to see if he was different from the rest of us. And he was different, sort of. Leaning back in his chair, he seemed to suggest, in a bored kind of way, that in the event of a US standoff with Russia, Putin nuking London would be the sort of collateral damage Washington could tolerate. A bit of an odd thing to say to a stranger. He didn’t observe the usual rules of conversation but rather, like a Roman emperor waiting to be entertained, remained belligerently aloof.

items.title: Vance scraps schedule to address tech outages as Trump admin insists incidents aren't linked
items.summary: Recent disruptions include a nationwide ground stop, Microsoft Outlook outage and a reported blackout of the National Security Agency's communications network.
items.body: Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday abruptly canceled his scheduled appearance at The New York Times DealBook Summit to instead attend meetings on a recent wave of high-profile technology outages . The cancellation was announced shortly after a senior Trump administration official insisted that the outages, which have affected a wide range of industries and have been felt across the country and around the world, are not the result of a cyberattack or any form of coordinated action. "We have a great deal of confidence in our assessment that these incidents are the result of upgrades of the systems, systems being patched, hardware being applied" or other "disparate" events, the official said on condition of anonymity to discuss the government's intelligence assessments.

items.title: Tech outages are causing people to panic-buy. Costco is benefiting, Mizuho says
items.summary: Shoppers are spending more at Costco as tech outages turn into a race to get emergency goods.
items.body: In the final week of October, Mizuho estimates, Costco's U.S. comparable sales, excluding gasoline, rose 11% to 12%, up from the normal 6% to 7% the first three weeks in October. Costco reported an 8.1% increase for the month. The firm said the stronger pace is continuing through November, as 21 of the 26 high-ticket generators it tracked on Costco's website sold out as of Sunday night. Shares of Costco were roughly flat-to-lower in Wednesday morning trading at around $1,107 apiece. "Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at COST," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger said in a research note Monday. Bellinger will appear on CNBC's "The Exchange" during the 1 p.m. hour.

items.title: Cathedral's staff review 'difficult but necessary'
items.summary: Gloucester Cathedral has been going through a restructure due to "significant financial pressure".
items.body: There will be no compulsory redundancies at a cathedral despite a restructure of staff, leaders have said. Gloucester Cathedral, which costs about £10,500 a day to open, has been undergoing an organisational restructure due to rising costs as some staff have opted for voluntary redundancies. It comes after cathedral bosses across the West of England said they had also been feeling the pinch, forcing them to find creative ways to raise money. Dean of Gloucester Reverend Andrew Zihni said the decision to reshape the cathedral's money was "difficult but necessary" to ensure its future. Cathedral chiefs said the restructure involved a review of staff roles and responsibilities, as well as how the organisation is run. A small number of staff had been made voluntarily redundant as a result of the changes.

items.title: Will the Milburn review come good or go south? Either way, we’ll always have Eurovision
items.summary: The announcement of state plans to engage with young people told us nothing we hadn’t already heard, but it still felt momentous It’s one of the country’s worst kept secrets. There can’t be anyone left who hasn’t heard of Alan Milburn’s Neets review, let alone read most of it…
items.body: I t’s one of the country’s worst kept secrets. There can’t be anyone left who hasn’t heard of Alan Milburn’s Neets review, let alone read most of it too. It feels as if it’s become part of the fabric of our society for the past six months. There will be a Neets-shaped hole in our lives when it’s over. Not a day has gone by without some part of it being leaked to the media. Seldom has a pitch been so icomprehensively rolled. Milburn has been out and about giving interviews to everyone – regardless of whether they wanted one or not. I rather suspect the reason Royal Mail lied about calling to collect my parcel return yesterday was because the driver found himself cornered by Milburn for a couple of hours and was unable to complete his round. Either that, or Royal Mail has a fleet of vans crisscrossing the country whose sole purpose is to make sure they never deliver anything. Ghost vans.

items.title: Jeffries wins Democratic House speaker race, on track to make history in January
items.summary: Jeffries will still need to win a floor vote in January to officially become House speaker.
items.body: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won the nod from his caucus to become the next speaker of the House of Representatives. Jeffries, D-N.Y., still needs to be officially elected when the new Congress convenes in January. But he appears to be on a glide path to winning the gavel after Democrats voted 251-11 to nominate him, according to a person familiar with the vote who asked not to be named because the meeting was private. The win for Jeffries comes after months of debate over whether Democrats would stand by their existing leadership or oust them amid a progressive tide. Democrats trounced Republicans in the midterm elections and are poised to hold at least 257 House seats. Jeffries would make history as the first Black speaker of the House if he is elected in January.

items.body: T houghts and half-price prayers with Poundland, please. The discount chain has been on the verge of collapse for a while , and its future looks bleak. Now, to add to the ignominy, David Beckham is kicking it while it’s down. Not literally, by the way: I suppose I should spell that out since we’re dealing with a litigious billionaire . I did not mean to imply or cause a reasonable person to infer that Sir David is standing on Brixton high street kicking a Poundland. Rather, DB Ventures, the licensor of the David Beckham brand, is causing a bit of a stink about the fact that the football legend’s fragrance range was found on sale in the discount store as well as at other purveyors of budget goods. It is now suing the perfume company , Coty, which it further accuses of under reporting sales, for $41m (£31m).

items.title: Target shares rise 7% as retailer posts best sales growth in five years, hikes guidance
items.summary: Target beat third-quarter sales expectations and raised its guidance as it continues a turnaround effort.
items.body: Target on Wednesday reported its best sales growth in more than five years and beat Wall Street's revenue expectations, the latest signs of its turnaround strategy taking hold. The retailer said its net sales grew 7.1% during the fiscal third quarter. Comparable sales rose 5.6%, compared with StreetAccount estimates of up 3.8%. That growth was boosted by a 5% increase in comparable traffic, Target added. "[It's] a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often," CEO Michael Fiddelke told reporters. Encouraged by the growth, Target raised its full-year guidance, upping its net sales growth guidance by 1 percentage point to around 6%. It's also expecting full-year operating income margin rate to be around 6.2%, which includes roughly 1.1 percentage points of benefit from tariff refunds.

items.title: We made GTA 6, the world’s biggest video game – we should have working conditions to match | Nestor Uriarte
items.summary: After the release of Grand Theft Auto VI this week, Rockstar employees like me can make history again. We need union recognition to safeguard our jobs When I first got the call offering me a job at Rockstar, I was thrilled. I thought back to being a child and sneaking into my…
items.body: W hen I first got the call offering me a job at Rockstar, I was thrilled. I thought back to being a child and sneaking into my brother’s room to grab the PlayStation Portable so I could secretly play Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories. The same kid who fell in love with Rockstar’s games back then now gets to spend every day helping to create those worlds as an animation programmer at the studio in Edinburgh. This week, we will celebrate the culmination of more than a decade of effort: the release of the most anticipated game of all time, Grand Theft Auto VI . But our team has the opportunity to make history a second time this month. Right now, the ballot is open for Rockstar employees to decide whether we want the union we have built with our colleagues to get recognition.

items.title: Nvidia sinks after earnings, dragging down neoclouds CoreWeave, Iren
items.summary: Nvidia's earnings come at a tumultuous time for the company.
items.body: Nvidia shares declined another 2.89% Wednesday after the company issued its first earnings report since the departure of former CEO Jensen Huang . The stock is down more than 13% over the past week. Trading in the neocloud companies was volatile throughout the day, as CoreWeave closed down 4.13%, Iren sank 3.61% and Nebius whipsawed, ending the trading day up 0.87%. Nvidia's third-quarter revenue came in at $115.84 billion, more than $6 billion above analysts' expectations of $109.10 billion, while fourth-quarter guidance of $130 billion topped the $125.1 billion consensus, according to LSEG. The semiconductor giant continues to navigate the fallout from Huang's resignation last week.

items.summary: About 23,000 households use heating oil in Northumberland and face increasing bills this winter.
items.body: An MP has urged a council to speed up the process of heating oil support payments as energy prices soar. About 23,000 Northumberland homes use oil systems as they are not connected to the mains gas supply. Labour's North Northumberland MP David Smith said a freedom of information request from 21 September showed just over a third of households who applied for help with heating oil costs had received funding from Northumberland County Council. However, the Conservative-led local authority said its latest figures showed significantly more applications had now been approved almost two months on. Unlike gas, oil prices are not protected by the Ofgem Energy Price Cap, and households have experienced huge increases in the cost of filling tanks.

items.title: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
items.summary: The telehealth company will now offer compounded forms of sermorelin, glutathione, NAD+, vitamin B-12 and L-carnitine, none of which are approved by the FDA.
items.body: Hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators. Even as it announced the new products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space. The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.

items.title: Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.summary: Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly…
items.body: Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster. Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the ouster of Huang over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with his own employees. Following the tumult, Nvidia’s stock tumbled more than 10%, shedding hundreds of billions in value and dropping its valuation to $3.7tn. In October, the company had hit an all-time-high valuation of nearly $6tn, but its share price has steadily fallen since then amid a broader AI slowdown.

items.title: With Jensen Huang gone, Colette Kress shows Nvidia is still at the center of AI
items.summary: In her first earnings report as interim CEO, Nvidia's Colette Kress calmed investors' nerves, at least for the moment.
items.body: Five days after Nvidia 's Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded 33 years ago under a cloud of scandal, a nervous base of shareholders eagerly awaited Colette Kress' first public appearance as interim CEO. Following Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings report on Tuesday, Kress offered some relief to Wall Street, at least temporarily, by proclaiming on the call with analysts that customers are still fully onboard and that there's no slippage in demand. She said leadership from Nvidia's most important supplier, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company , visited company offices this week. "We've engaged with our customers, we've engaged with our suppliers, our partners, they're all 100% behind us," Kress said on the call.

items.title: Brexit work travel rules need urgent improvement, say UK business leaders
items.summary: CBI says restrictions on cross-Channel work trips are hindering investment and trade between UK and Europe Business chiefs have called on the UK government and the European Commission to urgently ease Brexit restrictions on business travel for cross-Channel work trips. A group…
items.body: Business chiefs have called on the UK government and the European Commission to urgently ease Brexit restrictions on business travel for cross-Channel work trips. A group representing industry bosses said it wants commitments from Andy Burnham and European political leaders that the restrictions will be one of the priorities in 2027 for furthering ties between the two sides, after a summit in Brussels this week. The Confederation of British Industry (CBI), which represents some of Britain’s largest companies, welcomed the prime minister’s recent calls for a reset with Europe, designed to reverse some of the damage to Britain’s economy caused by Brexit. But it said Brexit restrictions, which include making employees obtain work permits for travel, are deterring cross-border investors and hampering trade at the very time both sides are trying to build resilience against China.

items.title: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
items.summary: Jensen Huang will appear before the Senate banking committee, its Chair Tim Scott said. That adds to an already announced appearance before House panels.
items.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, panel Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify, Scott said. The agreements to appear voluntarily come as pressure builds on Capitol Hill to investigate Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which led to his ouster at the chipmaker he founded. "They both have agreed," Scott said. "We will hopefully have this done before Christmas." Huang reached an agreement on Tuesday with the chairmen of three House committees for a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1 jointly before the three panels. Scott had asked Huang to appear publicly in the Senate. A spokesperson for the banking committee did not immediately respond to questions about when Huang and Lutnick would testify.

items.summary: The dispute comes ahead of a planned meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping.
items.body: Germany and the U.K. have pushed back against U.S. criticism of Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, underscoring tensions between Washington and European allies over Kyiv's war strategy. The clash comes ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral meeting on Thursday between U.S. President Donald Trump , Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China. Geopolitical flashpoints such as trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons are expected to be a major focus of Trump, Putin and Xi's meeting, with external observers closely monitoring any discussion of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. items.title: Gamers 'become' New Zealanders for first access to new 'Grand Theft Auto'
items.body: CANBERRA -- The launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," the latest title in the blockbuster video game series, as the clock ticks past midnight later Wednesday, is shaping up to be the largest entertainment product release on record and, for several hours, New Zealand will be the place to be -- or at least pretend to be.
